question: Candidates rejected for a broken binding were simulated to the interval horizon. Step 1: stop early, charge as before (structural). Step 2: charge only frames simulated (behavioural).

protocol.cpu: Process CPU (user+system) of one compileHandoff per process, LR_ENGINE=wasm, as docs/research/speed-20261029.json: each pair runs both arms concurrently with alternating launch order; the five cases run side by side; step-1 and step-2 pair sets ran at the same time. Only paired ratios are compared.
protocol.panels: npm run eval, --panel=dev and --panel=confirm (48 cases: 4 songs x 4 seeds + 2 perturbations each), standard budget, strike3. Step-1 runs remeasured under the step-2 measurement identity with tools/eval/remeasure.ts (every field reproduced). Paired song means, 4000-draw song bootstrap (tools/eval/summary.ts).
protocol.counters: Scratch-instrumented copies only (never committed): crashes, frames after the first unbound frame, frames skipped, and crashes whose stop had to wait for an own-line collision.

gates.engineTrace: synthetic-200 identical (baseline recorded at ef917b1e, equal to the main checkout trace)

step1.nativeTestMutation: Stopping at the crash when it was not on the candidate own lines: a sibling read then costs 69 more frames (total 149 vs 80) in tests/native_binding_stop.test.ts geometry.

hypothesis.text:
Step 2 hypothesis (written 2026-10-30, before any step-2 code or run)

Change: a candidate whose rider or sled comes unbound stops at the first unbound
frame (whether or not it has touched its own lines) and is charged only the frames
it simulated. Step 1 stays the baseline: it has identical tracks, frame counts
and scores to the current default, so the comparison isolates the accounting.

Mechanism: frames that were charged but not needed (post-crash frames, measured
by step 1's counters) stay in the allowance. The adaptive prefix width and local
sampling schedule spends remaining allowance on further candidate evaluations.

Predictions, paired by case against step 1 on the dev panel and on the confirm
panel (fresh seeds 505-808, perturbations 3-4), 48 cases, 4 songs:
1. Completion: unchanged (both arms expected to complete every case).
2. v3 impact loss: equal or lower (paired song-mean difference <= 0).
3. Not worse beyond the song-bootstrap interval: v3 strong / very strong / quiet
   bias, air rms, speed rms, amplitude rms, contested strong beats, strong extra
   impacts (v3), strong arrivals inverted/backward, body drag, off-beat kicks.
4. Physics frames (charged = simulated in step 2): about the same as step 1,
   because the search spends its allowance; so CPU per compile rises back toward
   the current default's, giving back most of step 1's CPU saving.

Prior: the effect is probably small or null. Earlier work found results not
monotone in budget, and a 1.5x allowance gave no gain on amour.

Decision rule: recommend step 2 only if completion is not worse, v3 impact loss
is lower on both panels (authored rides, paired song mean < 0), and no ruler is
worse with its 95% song interval excluding zero. Otherwise recommend step 1
alone, which keeps its CPU saving with identical tracks. No constant is tuned.
hypothesis.note: Written before any step-2 code or run (scratch file hashed at that time).

testFixtureRecalibration.method: nearest allowance (50/2500-frame steps) reproducing every original assertion under step 2

catalog.interpretation: Training-catalog robustness (benchmark/v4, 168 cases x 2 seeds, the Oct 5 audit work list), not held-out music. Equal source-group weight, group bootstrap over 15 groups. Completion over all compiles; quality on cases complete in both arms.
catalog.protocol: Scratch worker compiling each benchmark/v4 case as tools/research/value_collect.ts does (same filter and seeds, productionBudget, line.strike.v3, explicit plan or creative {} with phrase starts), measured with tools/eval/measure.ts and summarized with tools/eval/summary.ts. Work list identical to quality-20261005-catalog.json (336 id/seed/input hashes). 20 jobs per arm, both arms concurrently.
